# Carbonara

## Ingredients

- 200 g guanciale, cut into thick lardons
- 400 g spaghetti or rigatoni
- 4 egg yolks plus 1 whole egg
- 80 g pecorino romano, finely grated
- a heavy hand of freshly ground black pepper
- salt for the water

## Steps

1. Render the guanciale in a cold dry pan over medium heat until the fat runs and the edges crisp. Kill the heat.
2. Whisk the 4 yolks and the whole egg with the pecorino and plenty of black pepper into a thick paste.
3. Boil the pasta in lightly salted water until just shy of al dente. Keep a mug of the cooking water.
4. Toss the drained pasta in the guanciale pan off the heat, then stir in the egg mix, loosening with pasta water until it turns glossy.
5. Serve at once with more pecorino and another crack of black pepper.

## Notes

There is no cream in carbonara and there never should be. The silkiness comes from eggs, cheese, starch and pork fat. If the pan is too hot the eggs scramble, so pull it off the heat before they go in. I use the rendered guanciale fat, not butter. The dish waits for no one, so warm the bowls. I grate the pecorino romano on the microplane so it melts into the eggs without a single lump. The pan must be warm but never hot, and I stir constantly so no strand of pasta sits still long enough to scramble. A splash more pasta water brings it back if the sauce tightens on the way to the table.
